title: How to find shipper leads and build your own prospect list.
seoTitle: How to find shipper leads and build your own prospect list
searchIntent: How do freight brokers find and qualify shipper leads?
excerpt: Build a useful shipper list through product research, contact verification, and appropriate follow-up with facilities you have served.
takeaway: A prospect list is more valuable when you understand why each company belongs on it and how to begin the conversation.

sections.title: Choose a starting industry for the research session.
paragraphs: Luis’s lead-building demonstration starts with an industry rather than a purchased collection of names. The choice gives the search direction; it does not have to define the brokerage forever. Learn the products and businesses within that starting area, then follow the useful connections.

The recorded example begins with agriculture and fertilizer. Product terms such as ammonia, urea, ammonium nitrate, and diesel exhaust fluid reveal related chemical-manufacturing opportunities. Those terms make the search more specific than simply looking for any company that might ship freight.

sections.title: Use a large business to learn the product vocabulary.
paragraphs: A large company can be a research starting point even when it is not the account you intend to pursue. Study what it produces and how the products are described. Then look for related manufacturers, distributors, and businesses working with the same materials.

This is where research develops a skill that a purchased list cannot supply by itself. You begin to recognize which businesses belong together, what they may move, and which questions are still unanswered. The list becomes an organized result of that understanding rather than a substitute for it.

sections.title: Narrow the company and contact search.
paragraphs: In the historical demonstration, Luis filters by industry, geography, relevant logistics titles, and company size. His example uses a headcount below five hundred. That is a targeting choice from the lesson, not proof that a company has freight available or that its buying process will be simple.

Use the tools available to identify likely contacts, then confirm the important details against the company’s own information. The recorded interface may change over time. The durable process is to narrow the search, identify the role, and verify the contact path before outreach.

sections.title: Record information that makes the next action possible.
paragraphs: Luis’s working list includes the person’s name and role, professional profile, company, website, phone number, product information, and notes. These fields support a conversation. A name and number without context still leave the caller needing to do the research.

His demonstration finds conflicting phone numbers and checks the actual company website. That small detail illustrates the larger method: cross-check information instead of assuming a list provider or search result is current. Build the list in manageable research batches and qualify the entries as you go.

sections.title: Understand the limits of buying a shipper list.
paragraphs: The related lesson raises three concerns about purchased lists: several buyers may contact the same people, information can become stale, and relying on the list can prevent you from learning how to research. These are practical risks to evaluate, not proof that every list is fraudulent.

Even if you acquire contact data, the preparatory work remains. You still need to understand the company’s freight, identify decision responsibility, and establish a relevant reason to call. A larger file does not automatically create a better sales process.

sections.title: Consider appropriate follow-up with facilities you have served.
paragraphs: Another lesson discusses pickup and delivery facilities where the brokerage has genuinely handled freight. When appropriate, accurately referencing that work can create a more informed introduction to the facility’s shipping or logistics team. Ask whether it controls other transportation needs rather than assuming that it does.

Use this approach only when it fits the customer relationship and confidentiality commitments. Do not invent a prior shipment or disclose another customer’s private information. The useful principle is that real operational familiarity can support a conversation; it is not permission to solicit every facility without considering the existing relationship.
